data.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
data.description:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we're a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It's faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.

We're backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 6,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own the positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategy for core areas of Paddle's product suite.

This is a high-impact individual contributor role at the heart of our marketing function. You will be the connective tissue between Product, Sales, and Marketing translating deep customer and market insight into commercially sharp narratives that drive awareness, conversion, and revenue.

You'll shape how we go to market, how we equip our sales teams to win, and how we position Paddle for differentiation. The most successful candidate will be a master at aligning launch objectives to commercial value, connecting every GTM motion directly to business outcomes. Operating with a high degree of autonomy, you'll lead complex cross-functional workstreams, use data and AI-powered tools to accelerate your craft, influence strategic decisions, and mentor peers across the team.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of strategy and craft: a rigorous thinker who can also write a killer one-pager, run a crisp competitive briefing, and land a product launch with measurable impact.

What you'll do

Own positioning and messaging
- Develop and maintain differentiated positioning and messaging for key product areas, grounded in deep customer, market, and competitive insight.

- Translate complex product capabilities into clear, compelling narratives tailored to distinct buyer segments and personas.

- Ensure message consistency across all touchpoints website, sales collateral, campaigns, and executive communications.

Drive go-to-market strategy and execution
- Lead end-to-end GTM strategy for major product launches, from discovery and segmentation through to launch and post-launch measurement.

- Define launch objectives, success metrics, and cross-functional plans in partnership with Product, Sales, and Marketing teams always anchored to commercial & business outcomes

- Tie every launch plan directly to commercial value: align messaging, timing, and channel mix to where deals are won and revenue is made.

- Continuously improve GTM playbooks based on performance data, win/loss signals, and pipeline impact learnings.

Enable the commercial team
- Create high-impact sales enablement materials including pitch decks, battlecards, objection-handling guides, demo narratives, and ROI tools that equip Sales and Customer Success to win, expand, and defend revenue.

- Run training sessions and competitive briefings to keep the commercial team sharp and confident on product differentiation.

- Measure enablement effectiveness through content adoption, win rate trends, and deal velocity and use those signals to sharpen the assets over time.

- Partner with Revenue Operations to embed commercial messaging into the sales process and CRM workflow.

Be the voice of the customer and market
- Design and run qualitative and quantitative research programmes (win/loss interviews, customer surveys, persona studies) to develop a deep understanding of buyer motivations, pain points, and decision-making.

- Own competitive intelligence for your product area, tracking competitor moves, synthesising insights, and equipping the business to respond.

- Surface customer and market insights to influence product strategy and roadmap prioritisation.

Shape category and brand narrative
- Contribute to Paddle's broader category positioning and thought leadership strategy in collaboration with Brand and Content teams.

- Partner with the executive team on key narratives for analyst relations, investor communications, and major industry moments.

Measure and prove commercial impact
- Own the PMM measurement framework for your area: define success metrics for positioning work, product launches, and sales enablement that connect directly to business outcomes

- Leverage data to track launch performance, content usage, win/loss trends, and competitive displacement and use those insights to make better decisions faster.

- Work with Revenue Operations and Analytics to model the commercial impact of GTM initiatives and clearly articulate the ROI of positioning and research programmes to senior stakeholders.

- Bring a data-first mindset to every strategic decision: use quantitative signals alongside qualitative insight to prioritise, adjust, and prove impact.

Accelerate with AI and agents
- Use AI tools and agents actively to compress research cycles from competitive monitoring and win/loss synthesis to persona development, message testing, and brief generation.

- Build AI-assisted workflows that accelerate content creation and sales asset production without sacrificing quality or strategic rigour.

- Experiment with emerging agentic tooling to automate repeatable PMM tasks, freeing capacity for higher-leverage strategic work.

- Share AI workflows, prompts, and best practices with the wider PMM team to raise productivity and capability across the function.

Mentor and raise the bar
- Act as an informal leader and mentor to more junior PMMs, sharing frameworks, reviewing work, and helping the team grow.

- Contribute to the development of team processes, playbooks, and standards that improve the quality and velocity of PMM output.

We'd love to hear from you if you are

- An experienced product marketer with 8+ years in B2B SaaS product marketing, ideally in payments, fintech, or developer/platform tooling.

- A masterful storyteller who can distil complex, technical concepts into messaging that resonates with both technical and business buyers.

- Commercially sharp, with strong instincts for how product positioning translates into pipeline and revenue and a proven track record of tying GTM strategy to measurable commercial outcomes.

- A master at aligning launch objectives to commercial value: you connect positioning decisions to where deals are won, where revenue is lost, and what moves the number.

- Highly autonomous and structured, able to manage multiple complex workstreams simultaneously and deliver to a high standard with limited oversight.

TL;DR: Lovable's growth marketing runs on creative. The volume, variety, and quality of concepts we put in front of people, and how fast what we learn from them turns into the next round. Your job is to own that loop end to end, constantly iterating on it to achieve the best results against your KPIs.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we’re looking for

  • You've run high-volume creative testing on performance marketing and can talk specifically about what you learned, not just what you shipped.

  • You use AI tools daily and have built something with them that other people now depend on. A workflow, an agent, an internal tool, a tagging pipeline.

  • You have opinions about what makes an ad work and can articulate them well.

  • You write well for ads. Briefs, hooks, scripts etc.

  • You're comfortable being wrong in public. A lot of tests lose, and the loop only works if we’re all comfortable with that.

  • You move fast, but balance that with exceptional craft and know where the balance is.

What you’ll do

You'll be the person who decides what we test, why, and what the results mean. Then you'll build the workflows that turn those answers into hundreds of assets a month without losing the taste that made them work in the first place.

  • Own the creative operating system. You run creative ops for performance marketing: intake, briefing, production, QA, launch, and post-mortem. You'll define how the process works and then automate the parts that don't need a human in the loop.

  • Be the creative performance decision maker. When we can produce hundreds of creatives, you’ll be the person to judge what we make more of, what gets killed and what to slightly edit. That means holding the creative standard high, and making sure that creatives generated look Lovable.

  • Build agentic workflows and keep improving them. You'll design pipelines that generate, adapt, and localise creative at volume, with evals to check quality before anything ships. When a workflow breaks, you diagnose it and help rebuild it.

  • Turn performance data, audience insights and product knowledge into concepts. You'll dig into what's actually driving results, hook, format, message, subject, pacing, offer, and separate the signal from the noise a low-spend winner creates.

  • Run brainstorms and briefing. You own the rhythm that takes learnings, customer language, competitor moves, product releases, and additional context, and works with the wider team to turn them into briefs.

  • Push learnings across the company. What wins on paid usually tells us something about the website, lifecycle emails, App Store listings, and organic content. You'll be the one making sure that reaches the relevant people so we become more informed collectively.

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

data.description:
Revenue Operations Manager

📍 Manchester, UK (Hybrid 2 days WFH) | 💰 Up to £70,000


Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everyone by elevating UK estate agencies through world-class technology.


Your job is to own the numbers for the entire commercial engine. Not hit them, own them. You'll build the single version of the truth that runs our marketing, sales and customer success functions, and put a reliable set of numbers in front of our leadership team and board.


You will take accountability for the integrity of the full commercial funnel from top-of-funnel marketing through to churn and renewals. Right now, each function applies its own definitions and rules. You'll set one consistent set of rules and make them stick across the entire business. You'll also be responsible for forecasting, headcount planning and supporting the design of commission structures.


This is a hands-on, senior operator role. You'll own the tech stack (HubSpot sits at the centre), and you'll build the workflows, automations and permissions that keep data clean at source. You're not tidying records by hand; you're designing systems. You'll also be working with AI daily – it's not optional here. We use Claude, and you'll need to show evidence of AI already embedded in how you work.


There are no commissions or bonuses in this role and that is deliberate. The role has to stay objective about what the figures say. We've positioned the salary to reflect both your seniority and the independence you'll need to challenge senior leaders professionally and diplomatically when the numbers don't match the narrative.

HERE'S WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT TO BE WORKING ON


  • Building and maintaining complete visibility across the entire revenue line: marketing pipeline, sales pipeline, churn and renewals, and capacity planning.

  • Setting and enforcing a single set of definitions and rules across marketing, sales and customer success, then making them stick.

  • Owning HubSpot end-to-end: permissions, day-to-day usage, workflow build, automations and the processes that keep data clean at source.

  • Producing forecasts, headcount plans and reporting that the leadership team can actually rely on.

  • Contributing to the design of commission plans and commercial structures.

  • Supporting the hiring and onboarding of a Sales Operations person, and training them to maintain what you've built.

  • Presenting to the board, with numbers that are clean, consistent and defensible.

  • Using AI to solve problems that would otherwise drown you in manual work.

  • Joining up the revenue line with the wider business (think product, finance, and marketing) so everybody's working from the same playbook.

WHY YOU SHOULD (AND SHOULDN'T) APPLY

YOU SHOULD APPLY IF:

  • You've owned reporting across a full commercial funnel (not just the sales pipeline). You can point to a forecast you owned, a commission plan you shaped and workflows you built yourself.

  • HubSpot is second nature to you. You operate at expert or power-user level and you can configure permissions, automations and processes without breaking into a sweat.

  • You've worked in multi-product SaaS at a senior level and you understand how different product lines affect pipeline, ARR and churn.

  • AI is already woven into how you work. You can give concrete examples of which tools you use, what you've built with them, and how they've changed your process significantly.

  • You can challenge senior leaders diplomatically but firmly, and you're not afraid to report the numbers as they actually are, not as people hope they'll be.

  • You work best with autonomy. You're a self-starter who gets the work done yourself, not someone who needs to manage others to feel productive.

  • You'd rather build something new than inherit a legacy system, and you're excited by the chance to define how commercial operations should work.


YOU PROBABLY SHOULDN'T APPLY IF:

  • You've spent your career managing the sales pipeline in isolation, without visibility into marketing and customer success.

  • You'd struggle with HubSpot or you'd need somebody else to handle the tech stack. This is not negotiable, unfortunately.

  • You need variable pay to feel motivated. Commission and bonus structures feel essential to you.

  • AI feels like a threat rather than a tool. You see it as something that reduces your value, not something that multiplies what you can deliver.

  • You need a large team beneath you from day one. This role starts solo and hands-on, though you'll build a team over time.

  • You'd rather build strategy than do the work. The first six months are about delivery—designing the systems, building the reports, making it stick—not sitting in planning meetings.


A BIT ABOUT YOU

Experience

You've spent time in a revenue operations, commercial operations or similar role, with demonstrable ownership of the full commercial funnel. You've done the work yourself – like configuring HubSpot, building forecasts, and leading alignment conversations across functions. Multi-product SaaS experience is non-negotiable; B2B exposure is strongly preferred.

 

Tooling

HubSpot sits at the centre, and you're an expert here. Experience with other platforms, such as Salesforce or Pipedrive, is a plus (some skills transfer). You're comfortable across other tech stacks and you use AI regularly as part of your workflow. Other tools in the stack will change and you're flexible on that front.


Communication

You can present to senior audiences without losing clarity. You push back on senior leaders when the numbers don't match the narrative, and you do it diplomatically enough that they listen rather than push back harder. You explain complex commercial logic in plain language.


Research

You think operationally. You diagnose what's broken in a process, you ask tough questions about data quality, and you can identify which problems to tackle first based on commercial impact. You're curious about how the business actually works, not just the metrics.

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everyone buying, selling, renting and letting property, improving the industry for all of them by elevating UK estate agencies through world-class technology.

If you join us, you'll be helping to improve the property industry for everyone by widening the reach of our products and introducing them to estate agents across the UK, in turn making agents more successful and helping them deliver an incredible customer experience. We'll support you with structured training, a competitive commission structure and an open, inclusive environment.

If you love autonomy, are naturally curious and want to have a genuine impact within a rapidly growing company, we think you'd fit right in!

Here's what you can expect to be working on as a Business Development Manager…

  • Building and managing a pipeline of potential clients, focusing on high-value opportunities.

  • Using a consultative sales approach to deliver Street demos that address each client's specific needs.

  • Proactively sourcing and nurturing leads to grow your pipeline and secure new business opportunities.

  • Ensuring a seamless handover to, and close collaboration with, our Customer Success team, to increase client ROI and reduce churn.

  • Sharing best practice and innovative approaches to B2B sales to enhance the effectiveness of the sales team.

  • Working closely with our development teams to provide fresh ideas on product development.

  • Ensuring our customers have a best-in-class experience at every opportunity.

  • You have solid experience in SaaS, CRM or an aligned industry, with a track record of B2B sales to decision-makers at all levels.

  • You consistently achieve and exceed sales targets through proactive prospecting and closing of deals.

  • You bring energy and enthusiasm to your work, helping to create a positive and motivating atmosphere during outbound sessions.

As a fast-moving and rapidly evolving tech company, we embrace the advantages of AI and encourage its use throughout our application process. data.title: Associate Relationship Manager - London
data.description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

Our vision is to reimagine Relationship Banking for established SMEs, through the very best people, products and digital tools. Allica’s Relationship Management team was formed in 2022 and continues to grow at pace, providing established SME customers with expert human relationships alongside modern banking technology.

The team supports customers with lending, current accounts, savings, asset finance and working capital facilities, while building deep local relationships with SME customers, trusted professional advisers and business communities.

The Associate Relationship Manager role is a newly created position that is a key step in our ambition to build the best Relationship team to support our SME clients. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of clients and be expected to deliver across a range of commercial, customer service and risk objectives whilst also providing support to the wider relationship team as part of their development.

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to develop their skills and progress a career as an SME Relationship Manager.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Manage a portfolio of SME customers delivering outstanding customer service, building genuine and trusting relationships and develop a deep understanding of your clients’ businesses and their ambitions.

  • Deliver against a range of commercial targets including lending and new customer / deposit acquisition, as well as identifying and meeting a range of client needs through the provision of Allica products and services.

  • Build a trusted external network with SME advisers and the wider business community. Leverage this network to generate new business opportunities for the bank, in addition to signposting your clients to external support and advice as appropriate.

  • Ensure that Risk is managed effectively on your portfolio, with all required risk activities completed on time and to a high standard. Use customer data and internal Allica systems to identify signs of client stress and take proactive action to tackle early.

  • Work closely with a Senior Relationship Manager, contributing to building a bespoke personal development plan which will include supporting them and the wider team as part of your learning.

  • Take an active role in new business campaigns, including attending events, following up on leads, supporting prospect engagement and undertaking some cold calling where appropriate.

  • Support event organisation and follow-up activity, helping the team build strong local relationships with SME customers, prospects, accountants, solicitors and other trusted professional advisers.

  • Maintain accurate CRM records, strong follow-up discipline and good control over customer, prospect and portfolio activity.

  • Build strong, collaborative and productive relationships with your team and wider internal stakeholders to ensure customer needs are meet efficiently and any issues resolved quickly.

Personal Attributes & Experience

  • Some B2B sales, account management and/or SME banking experience, with a clear interest in building a career in SME relationship banking and a passion for supporting SMEs to be more successful.

  • Some experience of commercial lending and understanding / analysing financial accounts would be of benefit.

  • Curious, proactive and keen to learn, with the motivation to develop lending, sales, risk management and portfolio management capability through formal training and on-the-job coaching.

  • Confident engaging with customers, prospects and SME business advisers (including in person, via video call and by phone) asking great questions, following up consistently and building professional relationships.

  • Good organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage customer information and requests, portfolio tasks and follow-up actions accurately and at pace.

  • Practical understanding of customer service, sales activity and account management disciplines, ideally gained in a B2B, financial services or relationship-led environment.

  • Confident using systems, CRM tools and data to manage activity, track progress and support strong customer and risk outcomes.

  • Experience using AI tools in a business environment would also be of benefit.

  • An energetic, resilient, hands-on approach, with the confidence to get into the detail, solve problems and take ownership of outcomes.

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to build credibility with customers, prospects, advisers, colleagues and stakeholders.

  • Strong alignment to Allica’s values, with the judgement, integrity and energy to lead by example and help contribute to the next phase of the Direct Relationship Management channel.

Working at Allica Bank

At Allica Bank we want to ensure our employees have the right tools and environment in which to succeed in their role and in support of our customers.

Our employees are at the heart of everything we do, so our benefits are designed with you in mind:

  • Full onboarding support and continued development opportunities

  • Options for flexible working

  • Regular social activities

  • Pension contributions

  • Discretionary bonus scheme

  • Private health cover

  • Life assurance

  • Family friendly policies including enhanced Maternity & Paternity leave

Don’t tick every box?

Don’t worry if you don’t have all the skills or requirements listed on the job description. If you think you’ll be a good fit, we’d still love to hear from you!

Flexible working

We know the ‘9-to-5’ isn’t right for everyone. That’s why Allica Bank is fully committed to flexible and hybrid working. Please let us know what is best for you and, if we can, we will do our best to accommodate.

Diversity

We’re a diverse bunch here at Allica, with all kinds of experiences, backgrounds and lifestyles. Our openness and differences make us stronger, and we want everybody to feel comfortable bringing as much of themselves to work with them as they like.

data.description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Allica Bank aims to provide Expert Banking for Business Britain by providing excellent customer experience and pioneering technology solutions to facilitate this.

The Autonomous Lending tribe runs across multiple business lines including Credit Operations and Underwriting, with a mission to build AI-first lending origination journeys, automating origination capabilities, data flows, and underwriting and operational workflow management.

The tribe is a critical driver for Allica to continue to realise its vision of providing a market leading relationship-based banking experience, at a speed and cost to serve the rest of the market cannot match.

Role Description
The Product Owner will lead the work to define, deliver and manage AI-enabled products across our lending journeys, bringing together product design and thinking with a strong working knowledge of what today’s AI can and cannot do.

You will be accountable for the roadmap of your team and for the full product lifecycle: discovery and design, day-to-day delivery, launch and adoption by colleagues and customers, and how risks are addressed once a product is live. You will aim to build robust, automated and well-governed systems and processes that enable us to move quickly and innovate our lending and financing products in the SME banking market.

Whilst a lot of the market aims to avoid the complex nature of SME businesses, we are going for it head on, designing simple and efficient solutions to the most complex problems in the market to provide excellent and efficient customer experience. We aim for our external view of the lending product, as well as our internal systems to be the best in market which will allow us to scale quickly to serve more UK SMEs, while doing so in a cost-effective manner.

  • Responsible for innovation and building end-to-end solutions for AI-enabled lending product, origination, underwriting and operational flows

  • Lead a small cross-functional team (e.g. a full stack engineer and AI specialist) to deliver your roadmap

  • Continuously review business needs, refine priorities and iterate towards measurable outcomes – judged on fewer requests for further information, more applications decided with AI, less colleague time per application across underwriting and credit operations, and risk outcomes no worse than the equivalent manual journey

  • Prototype and experiment quickly – vibe-code working prototypes yourself, close enough to the real thing that an engineer can harden it into production code

  • Determine the accuracy of AI solutions by analysing the data yourself and building the verified “ground truth” datasets that results are tested against, working with underwriters and credit operations colleagues to agree what a correct answer looks like

  • Take responsibility for launch and adoption – briefing stakeholders, training the teams who will use the product, and closing the loop on the feedback they give back

  • Produce the written work that keeps delivery moving and safe – clear descriptions of what we are building and why, a record of the important design decisions and trade-offs made, and the assessments needed to get a product approved and live, covering risk, security, cost, data and legal considerations, and taking the change through the bank’s governance and approval process

Personal Attributes & Experience

  • Understanding of privacy and safety considerations when applying LLMs in production, and of how to prove and monitor accuracy once a solution is live – ideally in a regulated environment

data.description:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About the Role

This is not a traditional accounting role focused on maintaining legacy systems.

At Volta, you will help build the finance function from first principles, contributing to the design of processes, controls, and reporting in a business deploying capital at global scale.

Working closely with the Senior Financial Accountant and the wider Financial Accounting and Transactional Function, you will play a key role in delivering accurate financial reporting while supporting the build-out of a scalable, best-in-class accounting environment across multiple jurisdictions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the execution of the monthly financial close

  • Prepare and post accrual, prepayment, payroll, capex, revenue, and FX entries, among others

  • Prepare balance sheet reconciliations for review

    • Cash, AR, AP, fixed assets, other payables and receivables, equity

  • Support transactional processing

    • Approvals, audit trail, and clean ledgers

    • Intercompany accounting and cross charges

  • Support internal financial reporting

    • Assist in monthly reporting packages

    • Support the analysis of variance to budget and prior periods

    • Analyze financial data to identify trends, variances, and risks

    • Assist management with ad hoc reporting and partner with FP&A and other teams to ensure accurate and timely financial reporting

  • Assist in building and documenting financial controls, accounting policies, and governance frameworks

  • Track capital spend and asset capitalization

    • Maintain fixed asset register

  • Support external reporting

    • Prepare U.S. GAAP (and IFRS where applicable) external financial statements

    • Support external audits and act as a key point of contact for auditors

    • Prepare support for auditors

  • Contribute to the implementation and optimization of ERP/accounting systems

  • Assist with tax compliance, indirect tax (e.g., VAT/sales tax) returns, and regulatory filings across jurisdictions

  • Maintain and enhance the general ledger and chart of accounts

Requirements

  • CPA (or equivalent)

  • Audit background

  • 2–5 years of post-qualification experience

  • Strong technical accounting knowledge, including U.S. GAAP (IFRS exposure is a plus)

  • Experience with month-end close and financial reporting

  • High attention to detail and strong analytical skills

  • Ability to operate in a fast-paced, high-growth, capital-intensive environment

  • Strong Excel skills; ERP experience is a plus

Nice to Have

  • Experience in infrastructure, energy, or data center environments

  • Exposure to multi-entity, international accounting environments

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up environment

What Makes This Role Different

  • Build, not maintain: Help create processes and controls from scratch

  • Operate at scale: Work in an environment where decisions impact significant capital deployment

  • High ownership: Direct exposure to senior leadership

  • Low bureaucracy: Fast decision-making and clear accountability

data.description:
We are looking for a Data Scientist to join the Business Analytics team within Spotify’s Business Strategy and Insights organization. You will work with the Audiobooks Analytics Lead to help shape our global audiobooks strategy and improve the experience for listeners, creators, publishers, and authors.

In this role, you will use data analysis, experimentation, and statistical modeling to evaluate some of the most important opportunities facing our audiobooks business. Your work will span content and catalog strategy, discovery and recommendations, subscriber growth, and new product and commercial initiatives. You will turn complex questions into clear recommendations and help senior leaders make confident decisions.

You will collaborate with a distributed team of analysts, data scientists, business leaders, product managers, editorial partners, and engineers. At Spotify, you will have access to rich datasets and the autonomy to explore them creatively and rigorously. Above all, your work will help shape how the world listens to and discovers audiobooks.


What You'll Do
  • Develop data-driven strategies for audiobook catalog, content discovery, listener engagement, and subscriber growth.
  • Evaluate new product, content, licensing, and commercial opportunities through forecasting, scenario modeling, and impact measurement.
  • Partner with Editorial, Personalization, Product, Finance, and Business teams to improve title selection, recommendation quality, and the listener experience.
  • Design and analyze experiments, including A/B tests and quasi-experiments, to measure the impact of product and go-to-market initiatives.
  • Monitor the health of the audiobooks business, identify emerging opportunities or risks, and translate them into clear recommendations.
  • Develop reliable analytical datasets, tools, and reporting that make important insights accessible and repeatable.
  • Work with analytics engineering and data partners to improve data quality and create scalable ways of working.
  • Present findings and recommendations to senior leaders, influencing the direction of our product and business.

    • Who You Are
  • You have 3+ years of professional experience in data science or analytics, ideally in consumer technology, media, subscriptions, marketplaces, or a similarly complex business.
  • You are fluent in SQL and proficient in Python, R, or another programming language, with a strong grasp of statistical methods, experimentation, and causal inference.
  • You combine analytical rigor with strong business judgment and can cleanly extract the “so what” from complex analysis.
  • You are comfortable working through ambiguous problems, structuring open-ended questions, and identifying a practical path forward.
  • You enjoy collaborating with a wide range of cross-functional partners and can build trust across technical and non-technical teams.
  • You are an excellent communicator who can present complex findings clearly to senior leaders and audiences with different levels of technical knowledge.
  • You have a degree in Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.

AI enablement for the product team. The product tool stack. Claude (incl skills), Figma, Linear, Notion, Pylon, Mixpanel, Datadog, Granola, our AI tooling, whatever comes next. You own how it's configured, how it connects and how well it's used. Kill what isn't earning its licence. Run the evaluation when we need something new. Connect them up so nobody's copy-pasting between systems. And structure our sources of truth — roadmap data, decision logs, product knowledge — so agents can read them as well as people can.

Launch and release coordination. The product launch calendar, readiness criteria, and a reliable record of what shipped when. The important part is the join between what we build and how we sell it. Product Marketing owns the narrative and the campaign and marketing release timing; you own the reality underneath it. You’ll know the product inside & out, you’ll ensure that the thing we're announcing has actually shipped, works, is documented for internal teams and customer, and a customer can use it on day one. Nothing goes out before it's ready. Nothing meaningful ships without the market hearing about it.

Early access programmes. Alpha, beta and design partner programmes are how we de-risk what we build and how our best customers get a stake in the roadmap. They run informally today. As we sell to bigger and more demanding enterprises they need proper structure: who gets in, what both sides commit to, how feedback gets captured and routed, and what has to be true before something goes GA. You'll design that and mature it as our customer base does.

Top-level metrics. PMs own the detail for their own areas and should keep owning it. You own the layer above: our North Star and company-level product metrics, the key metric from each team pulled into one picture, kept current and actually looked at. Product comms, including the roadmap deck. The internal newsletter, release notifications, release tracking. As we ship faster this becomes the difference between a business that's aligned and one that's guessing — Sales, Customer and Marketing should never be surprised by something we've shipped. You'll also own our external-facing roadmap deck, used with prospects and customers and as an internal alignment tool.

Documentation. Integration guides, technical docs and product reference material that get used live in sales cycles and onboarding. You'll keep them accurate as the product grows, you’ll track their adoption and adjust.

We're hiring the first dedicated owner of Omnea's performance marketing.

But nobody's job is to work out what actually produces pipeline and then make more of it. That's this role: take what's already running, find the ROI, and professionalise it into something we can be proud of.

In one week you might work out why a paid campaign is generating leads that never convert, rebuild the landing page that's losing them, build a new LinkedIn audience off the back of our closed-won data, and show the exec team what the pipeline picture looks like.

If you want to run one channel and hand-off the numbers, this might not be for you. If you want to own the loop from spend through to pipeline, and have the data to prove what worked, it is.

You'll work closely with our digital agency partners, the field marketers running events in the UK and US, and the sales team who rely on the pipeline you generate.

What you'll own

Pipeline and performance

You'll build the picture of what marketing is actually returning, and you'll be the person with the answer when someone asks whether a channel is worth the money.

  • Own the pipeline number for our digital channels: how much, from where, and at what cost

  • Build and maintain dashboards in Dreamdata using sources like HubSpot and GA4

  • Track campaigns from first touch through to closed won, and use what you find to change what we run next

  • Run a proper testing cadence. Set the test, call the result, and stop the things that aren't working

  • Report on what the numbers mean, not only what they are

Paid

You own paid. Our agency handles campaign build and optimisation, and you set the direction they work to.

  • Own LinkedIn as our primary paid channel: audiences, target account lists, retargeting and sequencing

  • Build audiences from our own data: closed-won patterns, target accounts, product signals - rather than off-the-shelf targeting

  • Work with content and design teammates to produce compelling content

  • Make the case for more budget when the numbers justify it

Website and conversion

  • Own conversion across the site: forms, journeys, page structure, and what happens after someone clicks an ad

  • Build and update pages using our existing component library and CMS

  • Run an ongoing testing programme on the pages that matter, and work with the in-house design team on what comes next

  • Ship landing pages for campaigns and product launches, including forms and tracking

  • Keep tracking and attribution clean, so the reporting can be trusted

What we're looking for

  • Experience in a B2B marketing role, in-house or agency. We care more about what you delivered than where you did it.

  • You're commercial. You think in pipeline and cost per opportunity, not clicks and impressions, and you can tell the difference between a campaign that's busy and one that's working.

  • You know paid mechanics properly. Audiences, match rates, attribution windows, frequency. LinkedIn Ads specifically.

  • You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a report from scratch, spot when something looks wrong, and explain a trend to someone who wasn't in the weeds with you.

  • You've built pages in a CMS. Not from scratch in code — assembling pages from components, keeping them consistent, and getting the tracking right.

data.title: Staff Software Engineer, Dev Environments
data.description:
The Dev Environments team sits within DoorDash's Foundations group (Platform Engineering). We own the local and remote developer experience across the DoorDash group of companies supporting over 5000 engineers. Our mission is to enable engineering velocity, quality, and efficiency at significant scale by removing friction from the day-to-day developer loop: spinning up a working environment, getting code building, and getting feedback fast, whether the "developer" is a human or an AI agent.

As a Staff Engineer on Dev Environments, you'll be recognised as an expert across the dev environments space, covering both local and remote dev flows, devcontainers, IDE/remote backends, and how they all fit together, including owning accountability for outcomes that span multiple teams. You'll set technical direction for the team's roadmap, unblock deep cross-cutting technical problems other engineers can't resolve alone, and mentor senior and mid-level engineers. You'll partner closely with engineering leadership across the group to translate ambiguous, company-wide developer-experience problems into a concrete, sequenced technical strategy.

What You’ll Be Doing

Technical direction

  • Define the architecture for how thousands of engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo actually develop and ship code: local and remote dev containers, remote IDE/VM lifecycle, and the full local-to-remote loop.

  • Build monorepo dev tooling at scale. It's part of consolidating all the companies under DoorDash’s umbrella onto one global backend - you're setting the standard, not patching one org's tooling.

  • Provision production-shaped environments in seconds, keep state in sync over the network, and make a remote machine feel local, reliably and cheaply, at thousands-of-concurrent-engineers scale.

  • Expect to invent as much as you adopt: much of this is genuinely unsolved elsewhere in the industry.

  • Design for AI agents as first-class consumers of the environment, not an afterthought: sandboxes that spin up on demand, run in parallel, and are safe to hand a real repo.

  • Support agents launched from an IDE, a CLI, or a Slack message - with no laptop required to review and ship what the agent did.

Collaboration & leadership

  • Align teams that don't naturally sit adjacent to each other (e.g. Security, Infrastructure, Product Engineering) around unstructured, ambiguous problems where there's no existing playbook.

  • Mentor engineers at all levels: run design reviews; raise the engineering bar through code review, pairing, and architectural guidance when appropriate.

  • Help set the hiring bar: lead interview loops, help calibrate, and support onboarding of senior hires.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

Essential:

  • A track record of shipping production systems and leading cross-team initiatives with group level impact - comfortable owning delivery end to end, from design through to production and adoption.

  • Hands on fluency with the languages and tooling used to build developer tooling (e.g. Go, Python, TypeScript) and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform).

  • Experience managing compute via Kubernetes (multi-tenant workload isolation, autoscaling ephemeral workloads, cost management), or lightweight VM/sandbox technology (e.g. Firecracker).

  • Working knowledge of cloud networking, including securely and cost-effectively routing traffic across network boundaries (VPNs, service meshes, etc.)

  • Experience integrating LLM/AI tooling into developer workflows - e.g. Claude Code - both locally, and remotely.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication; able to influence senior stakeholders and align multiple non-adjacent teams without formal authority over them.

  • Experience building close working relationships with the engineering teams who consume your platform, not just the platform team itself.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in developer platforms or adjacent infrastructure: devcontainers, remote development, remote IDE backends, or developer workstation tooling.

  • Practical experience with JetBrains remote-backend flows, Codespaces/Codeserver-style products, or equivalent.

  • Experience with remote build/execution systems (e.g. BuildBuddy), or large-scale build caching.

data.title: S&O Manager - Rider Fraud
data.description:
About the role

This role will lead our approach to understanding and reducing courier/rider fraud and abuse across Wolt and Deliveroo. Combining data-led investigation with strong operational judgement, you will identify emerging risk patterns, understand the features of our operating models that may contribute to those risks, and assess their potential impact.

A key part of the role is turning insight into action. You will translate analysis into clear, proportionate policies and operational responses that protect platform integrity and customer outcomes, while remaining practical to implement and appropriate for the markets in which we operate. You will work closely with Legal, Public Policy, Product, Data Science and Operations to navigate complex legal and regulatory considerations and ensure our approach is effective, fair and robust.

Core responsibilities

  • Lead a programme of work to identify, assess and prioritise courier/rider fraud and abuse risks across Wolt and Deliveroo.

  • Translate identified risks into proportionate policy, process and operational responses, balancing risk reduction with customer outcomes, courier/rider experience and business practicality.

  • Lead the implementation, monitoring and ongoing refinement of fraud and abuse policies, with clear measures of effectiveness and residual risk.

  • Ensure policy approaches are developed with appropriate consideration of legal, regulatory, compliance and reputational implications.

What you’ll be doing

  • Build a deep understanding of our courier/rider operating models, incentive structures and end-to-end journeys to identify where fraud or abuse risk may arise, using data, operational knowledge and structured, hypothesis-led analysis.

  • Develop analytical approaches and key metrics to identify patterns, quantify impact, assess detection signals and measure the effectiveness of policy interventions over time.

  • Define new policies, or revise existing ones, in response to identified risks that may negatively affect customers, couriers/riders, the platform or the wider business.

  • Conduct impact and risk assessments, framing clear options and recommendations that consider effectiveness, operational feasibility, cost, legal and regulatory requirements, and potential unintended consequences.

  • Partner closely with Legal, Public Policy, Product, Data Science, Trust and Operations teams to shape business requirements, implement agreed responses and resolve complex trade-offs.

  • Establish effective ways of working across Wolt and Deliveroo so that emerging trends, priority risks and lessons from policy performance are identified early and shared with relevant stakeholders.

  • Lead cross-functional delivery from problem identification through to implementation, reporting and post-launch monitoring, adapting the approach as new evidence emerges.


What we’re looking for

  • 6+ years’ experience in fraud, risk, compliance, policy, operations, consulting or a related field.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to combine data, operational context and judgement to identify root causes and prioritise action.

  • Experience translating complex or ambiguous risk issues into practical policies, recommendations and implementation plans.

  • Experience navigating complex legal and regulatory landscapes and working constructively with Legal and Public Policy stakeholders.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to influence senior and cross-functional stakeholders and challenge constructively when needed.

  • Strong project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, prioritise effectively and drive delivery in a fast-paced environment.

  • Comfortable using AI-enabled tools appropriately to support analysis, hypothesis generation and problem solving.

 

Why Deliveroo

Our mission is to transform the way you shop and eat, bringing the neighbourhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops and riders. We are transforming the way the world eats and shops by making access to food and products more convenient and enjoyable. We give people the opportunity to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it.

We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of the most rapidly expanding industry in the world. We are still a small team, making a very large impact, looking to answer some of the most interesting questions out there. We move fast, value autonomy and ownership, and we are always looking for new ideas.

At Deliveroo we know that people are the heart of the business and we prioritise their welfare. Benefits differ by country, but we offer many benefits in areas including healthcare, well-being, parental leave, pensions, and generous annual leave allowances, including time off to support a charitable cause of your choice. Benefits are country-specific, please ask your recruiter for more information.

data.description:
About 1st Formations
At 1st Formations, we empower entrepreneurs to start, run, and grow their businesses with confidence.

Running a business shouldn’t be slowed down by company formation, statutory compliance, accounting, or payroll. From day one, these essentials should be seamless, reliable, and intelligently handled — freeing founders to focus on building and scaling.

We’re a leading UK provider of company formation and compliance services, building a modern, fully integrated technology platform that supports founders at every stage of their journey. Our platform brings together formation, compliance, accounting, payroll, and ongoing business support in one cohesive experience.

No stitched-together services.

No legacy workflows disguised as software.

Just a single, scalable platform built for ambitious founders who want to move fast, stay compliant, and grow with confidence.

Why Join Us Now?
You’ll be joining a business with strong momentum, clear direction, and real opportunity for progression.

  • £18m annual revenue, including £9m ARR

  • Over 1 million companies formed

  • Certified B Corp and Carbon Neutral Business

  • Forecast to grow 5x–10x over the next three years

The Role

We're looking for a people-first, Customer Onboarding Executive to set new clients up for success from the moment they join our Accounting-as-a-Service product. You'll own the onboarding experience - running structured welcome calls with new clients, walking them through what we do, what to expect from our team, and what their key obligations are as a business. This is a client-facing role at its core: you'll spend the majority of your time on video calls, building rapport with startup founders and small business owners and making a complex topic feel simple and reassuring.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead 30–45 minute structured onboarding video calls with new clients using a prepared script, covering our services, their statutory obligations, and what they can expect from us

  • Walk clients through their key responsibilities in a clear, jargon-free way, including relevant compliance milestones like filing deadlines, VAT and PAYE registration, and Corporation Tax

  • Give clients a guided orientation of their accounting tools (e.g. Xero), so they feel confident from day one

  • Identify additional services a client may need (e.g. payroll, VAT) and flag these internally for follow-up

  • Ensure all client details are accurately captured in internal systems

  • Document and hand over all relevant information to the Customer Service and Retention teams at the close of onboarding

  • Spot early risks (e.g. clients who seem disengaged or behind on setup) and escalate to relevant stakeholders

  • Contribute to refining the onboarding process and improving the client experience over time

What We're Looking For

  • Proven experience running client-facing onboarding calls, welcome calls, or structured video-based client sessions - this is the most important thing we're hiring for

  • A natural communicator: warm, structured, and able to put people at ease on a call

  • Comfortable following and adapting a prepared script while keeping the conversation feeling natural

  • Confident explaining processes and obligations to clients who are new to accounting and business admin

  • Basic familiarity with UK statutory requirements for small businesses (e.g. Corporation Tax, Self-Assessment, VAT thresholds, PAYE) - you don't need to be an accountant, but you should be able to explain these clearly to a first-time founder

  • Any experience with cloud accounting platforms like Xero or QuickBooks is a bonus. We will provide full training

  • Strong documentation habits and the ability to prepare clean handovers for internal teams

  • Comfortable managing several active onboarding processes simultaneously

     

What We Offer

  • £32,000–£36,000 salary and comprehensive benefits package

  • Hybrid working model (3 days in office; 2 days from home)

  • A genuine opportunity to shape and build processes from scratch

  • Clear progression pathways as the practice scales

  • A culture that values ownership, impact, and continuous improvement

data.title: Senior Customer Support Engineer
data.description:
About Fyxer

Since launching in May 2024 we've grown to $30 million in ARR. Fyxer is building an AI executive assistant that handles emails, scheduling and follow-up, freeing people in client-facing roles to focus on their customers.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the hardest technical tickets in the business end to end, including the customer conversation, from first report through to resolution

  • Dogfood Fyxer’s own products, give feedback, and influence our roadmap

  • Establish blast radius before escalating, because one customer reporting something is a ticket and forty-seven accounts in the same broken state is an incident

  • Call bug, incident or user error correctly and quickly, and declare it when it's an incident

  • Write escalations Engineering can act on without a single follow-up question, and stay on them until they land

  • Spot patterns across Linear and the queue, raising a tracker before the fifth report of something becomes the tenth

  • Reduce the need for your own role through runbooks, saved queries, Parahelp knowledge, and hands-on upskilling of our senior agents

Here's the honest version of why this role exists. In one recent three-month window we escalated 47 tickets to Engineering and two of them were resolved. Engineering is capacity-constrained, and a third of what we sent them was correctly deprioritised. So this isn't a role that escalates better, it's one that resolves. You'll be backed by strong Customer Success and Product Engineering teams, and given read-only access to our codebase through Cursor, to our data through our internal tooling, and to our production logs to do it.

What Success Looks Like

  • You resolve a growing share of technical escalations without Engineering ever being involved

  • Your escalations are complete, so Engineer can act on them quickly

  • You use AI and you catch it when it's wrong, before it reaches a customer

  • You hold a customer's confidence while you investigate, rather than handing them back to someone else

  • Our senior agents are visibly more capable six months in than they are today, because of you

  • You're the person the team wants on the ticket because they trust your judgement.

What You Bring

  • 3+ years in a technical support role within a SaaS or cloud-based company

  • API fluency: you can read an API reference, reason about authentication, and say what a 401 rather than a 500 tells you about where the fault sits

  • SQL you write yourself: given an unfamiliar schema you work out how the tables relate and write the join unaided

  • Comfortable in logs, following a request across services and working backwards from an error

  • Strong written communication, particularly to a customer who is unhappy

  • Experience with customer support tools such as Zendesk, Intercom, Jira, Linear, others

  • Startup-ready: adaptable, fast-moving, and hands-on

We're not asking for production engineering experience or a computer science degree. We care what you can do, not how you got there.

Location and other bits

  • Based in our Chancery Lane office in London, Monday to Thursday, with Fridays from home

  • Standard office hours

  • Benefits include: on-site gym, private medical, pension and lunch provided everyday

The Hiring Process

  1. Submit your CV (no need for a cover letter)

  2. We'll review it

  3. An initial call with someone from the hiring team to review your experience and motivation for joining (30 mins)

  4. A call with our Head of Customer Support on your experience and how you think technically (30 minutes)

  5. A live technical exercise (60 minutes)

  6. Meet more of the team (30 minutes)

For the exercise we'll give you access to a small example application, a database, an API and its logs, a couple of days ahead, along with three customer tickets. You don't need to solve anything in advance, and you're welcome to use whatever AI tooling you normally would, because that's how the job actually works. We'll be paying attention to how you check its answers.

Our Culture

Our culture is intentional. It stems from the fact we're in the race of our lives to reshape one of the largest AI opportunities that exist; email. There is only first or last.

We're going to win by:

  • An obsession around the fact that every second counts, we have to move fast with intensity and drive hard every day.

  • Never let it slide, be relentless in challenging yourself and others to strive for the best outcome.

This culture is intense; it requires focus and discipline. So we'll do everything we can to remove distraction, support your wellbeing, and reward your impact

data.title: Senior Software Engineer
data.description:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We’re already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $500m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why we’re hiring

  • We're post-PMF and revenue generating, launching in the US ahead of a Series A. Early enough that you'll shape how engineering works here, late enough that you're not gambling on whether the product works.

  • You'll own significant parts of the product and ship the things customers feel most. It's a regulated platform moving money across multiple jurisdictions, so the work has to be right and it still has to be fast.

  • We also want the bar to move while you're here. Senior engineers set the standard through the quality of what they ship, how they review, and the problems they choose to fix rather than work around.

  • Alongside that, we're rethinking how we build with AI. We use the tools, but we know there's a step change available to teams who redesign their whole workflow around them rather than adding AI to how they already work. If you've already done that somewhere else, you'll have a lot of room here.

What we're looking for

  • You've built and run non-trivial production systems, and you've learned what works in which situations rather than defaulting to one approach.

  • Strong architectural judgement. Most of our code is now written by an LLM, which means you need to own the decisions around it: how the system is structured, what the patterns are, whether the thing being built is the right thing at all. Our stack is Go, and if you learn quickly, not having written it isn't a problem.

  • A serious AI practice. You can talk specifically about how AI has changed the way you build, what it's actually made faster, and what you've shared with the teams you've worked in.

  • Directness. You give feedback when something isn't good enough and take it just as well.

  • Good instincts about what's worth doing. You know when something needs to be built properly and when it doesn't, and you push for the work that makes everyone around you faster.

Probably not for you if

You think the impact of AI on engineering is overstated. You'd rather be handed a fully specified ticket than question the brief. Or the learning curve across finance, compliance and multiple jurisdictions sounds like a chore rather than the interesting part.

data.title: Head of Design
data.description:
About Odin

Private markets are overdue a design transformation, and there is still no design-led company setting the standard for the category. Most products in the space look and feel like a bank statement from 2009. We’re looking for someone to help us change that.

Odin is building infrastructure for the future of private markets. We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should be putting it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legals and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We’re already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $500m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Mission

We’re looking for a senior design leader who combines exceptional visual craft with systems-level product thinking. You’ll play a central role in defining and elevating the customer experience at Odin as we prepare for a major US launch.

The scope here is intentionally broad. Your remit spans across product and visual brand identity. You’ll help evolve our brand identity alongside the founders, expressing the philosophy, ambition and cultural stance of a company that is rethinking what progress means and how we get there.

Working with our existing designer, our Head of Product and the wider product team, you’ll help set the design direction for the company, raise the quality bar and shape how design operates as we grow. You’ll bring experience and conviction to make strong design decisions quickly, while creating the systems, practices and feedback loops that allow consistently excellent work to scale.

You’ll remain close to the work: exploring complex problems, building and testing prototypes, speaking directly with customers and translating what you learn into polished, production-ready experiences. You won’t be stepping into a finished structure. You’ll be helping to shape the next stage of it.

Your remit spans both product and brand. You’ll turn complex, regulation-heavy workflows and dense interfaces into experiences that feel clear, intuitive and inevitable.

Your Must-Have Qualities

We value designers who combine rigorous reasoning, high agency, exceptional craft and deep customer empathy. You’ll succeed in this role if you are:

  • Deeply user-centric: You advocate for the customer and care about how people experience the product. You use interviews, data and observation to understand real behaviour—not just what users say.

  • Exceptional in your craft: You have a highly developed eye for composition, hierarchy, interaction and detail. You create polished, cohesive experiences and hold the shipped product to a very high standard.

  • Reasoned and curious: You challenge assumptions, ask sharp questions and look for root causes rather than applying surface-level fixes.

  • Decisive with strong judgment: You make thoughtful trade-offs between speed, quality, complexity and compliance. You explore enough to make an informed decision, form a clear point of view and move quickly.

  • High agency: You don’t wait for perfect information or detailed direction. You identify what needs to happen, bring others with you and take responsibility for moving the work forward.

  • Systematic about discovery: You build repeatable ways of learning from customers, test assumptions early and establish regular feedback loops rather than treating research as a one-off stage.

  • Clear and collaborative: You articulate your thinking simply, write clearly and give engineers the context and detail needed to build what was intended. You debate constructively, respond well to feedback and operate with conviction without ego.

  • Comfortable with complexity and ambiguity: You create structure from incomplete information and navigate technical, regulatory and operational constraints without losing momentum.

  • Outcome-driven: You care about what happens after something ships. You measure impact and ensure your work genuinely improves the customer experience, business outcomes or operational efficiency.

Your Experience

Must-Have

  • Deep product design expertise and exceptional judgment, with a proven track record of shaping complex products end to end.

  • In-house experience, with ownership of complete customer journeys rather than isolated screens.

  • Strong information architecture, interaction design and prototyping skills.

  • The ability to produce high-quality work at pace, make confident visual decisions and maintain a consistently high bar across the product.

  • Strong systems thinking, with experience designing complete workflows spanning user actions, communications, automations, permissions, operational processes and technical constraints.

  • Experience designing complex, multi-party products or working within regulated environments.

  • The ability to independently lead discovery, including customer interviews, assumption validation, prototyping, usability testing and iteration.

  • Experience establishing structured, repeatable customer-research and feedback practices.

By the end of the FTC you will have partnered with the team to deliver 4–5 leadership or senior high-impact hires. We may extend the contract depending on priorities, but this window is focused on closing the critical searches at pace.

About You

  • You’ve led multiple hiring processes at once, ideally in a fast-paced, early-stage environment where ambiguity, urgency and competing priorities are the norm

  • You have experience in talent operations and attention to detail – spotting blockers early, keeping things moving, and improving systems as you go

  • You’re a clear, intentional communicator across async, written and verbal channels – able to bring others with you and influence at a senior level

  • You lead confidently in ambiguity, surfacing risks, asking the right questions, and helping hiring managers move forward with aligned, quality decisions

data.description:
At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Generative AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn’t just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.

We're looking for someone who loves building automations, agents and workflows, and wants to point that instinct at People Ops. You'll own the data and systems behind our People Ops stack (HiBob, Ashby, Remote), and use that ownership as the foundation for turning slow, manual, multi-tool processes into things that mostly run themselves. This is a role for someone who'd rather ship a working automation this week and improve it next week than spend a month planning the perfect system - someone who gets a genuine kick out of making the unglamorous stuff disappear. You’ll bring expertise, energy, and commercial thinking to help us elevate our People processes.

Key responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and maintain automations, workflows, and AI agents across our People Ops tooling (HiBob, Ashby, Remote) - from a simple triggered workflow to a more sophisticated internal agent - turning multi-step manual processes into things that run themselves.

  • Own the data layer everything else depends on: keep HiBob/Ashby/Remote data clean, resolve integration and schema issues between systems, and treat data integrity as the foundation of what you build, not an afterthought.

  • Run new joiner onboarding end to end, but treat every manual step you touch twice as a candidate for automation, with the goal is to keep making the process faster and lighter-touch, not just execute it reliably.

  • Administer employee lifecycle changes (promotions, transfers, terminations) across systems, and build the guardrails - validation rules, alerts, review steps etc, that catch data errors before they become a downstream mess in payroll or compliance.

  • Process documentation: create and maintain SOPs, checklists, and playbooks for onboarding, offboarding, and systems admin current as processes evolve, so nothing lives only in your head.

  • Partner with relevant stakeholders on anything touching UK employment or compliance judgement calls while you build fluency here. You own the system and the escalation path, and that ownership shifts to you over time.

Your background:

  • You can genuinely build: hands-on with automation/workflow tools (e.g. Zapier, Make, n8n, Retool or similar), and you've actually built or configured AI agents.

  • You've worked with structured data and APIs enough to reason about schemas, integrations, and what breaks when two systems disagree with each other.

  • You're comfortable being the systems administrator of SaaS platforms: owning permissions, workflows, and integrations, ideally across an HRIS/ATS/EOR stack (HiBob, Ashby, Remote) or a comparable set of business systems.

  • You've worked in a high-growth environment, ideally remote and across multiple geographies, and you're comfortable working async across EMEA time zones.

  • Any exposure to People Ops, HR systems, or UK employment practices is a genuine bonus, not a

  • requirement - we're hiring for the builder instinct first, and will coach the domain knowledge.

You’ll Thrive Here If You…

  • You're an Owner. You don't wait to be told the onboarding flow needs fixing, you notice the friction and you just fix it.

  • You're Fast. You'd rather ship a working automation this week and improve it next week than spend a month designing the perfect one.

  • You like Simple. Your default build is the one with the fewest moving parts, not the most impressive one.

  • You find Surprising in the unglamorous stuff. You get a kick out of turning "someone does this by hand every month" into something nobody thinks about again.

  • You're Human, even with agents. You know the systems you're building sit behind someone's first week at a new job, or a colleague's benefits question — you design for that person, not just for the workflow diagram.

KPIs & Success Measures

  • Number and scope of manual People Ops processes automated, and time saved per cycle

  • HiBob / Ashby / Remote data accuracy rate

  • Time to resolve employee systems requests

  • Reduction in error rate flowing into compliance-relevant fields
